packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-13 - unverified image reading (first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. I opened only BRIEF.md, PROMPT.md and the image files (I also ran `sips` to get pixel dimensions of the images, and `ls` of the packet directory, which shows packet.json exists; I did not read it).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview, face 1)
- Black background, ruler across the top, colour checker lower right. Three separate small parchment fragments, not one leaf:
  (A) small rectangular scrap, upper left-centre (approx 2 x 2 cm by the ruler): two narrow columns of black textura with red words (rubrics) in it; left column lines end "...ierusale", "...captiua ...", "...in ierusa...", "...lem ...", right column has a red initial (looks like "D"?) and line starts "Sur..", "nu..", "dne"... Looks like small-format liturgical text in two columns.
  (B) wider rectangular fragment, upper right (approx 7 x 4 cm): heavily abraded/stained, red script at top edge and lower lines, black text faint; a horizontal fold/crease; reads as a strip with rubricated lines.
  (C) long curved narrow strip, centre (approx 10 cm long, 1.5 cm wide): a binding strip, with red initials/letters visible (a red "D"-like letter in the middle, red at top), black text mostly abraded; holes (sewing/nail) near top and bottom.
- Orientation of B and C in the overview is uncertain; A appears upright.

TILES: image-002..005 are native-resolution tiles of face 1 (image-001). image-002 = upper-left quadrant: fragment A whole, left part of fragment B, top of fragment C.

FRAGMENT A (image-002.jpg, lines counted from top of the fragment; viewed via crop-01.jpg, 3x enlargement)
Script: textura (black), red rubrics, very small format; two columns, both cut at outer edges. Between the columns a faint grey, later-looking vertical mark (numerals? looks like "3 3 ..." written vertically) - not text of the book, uncertain.
Left column (left edge cut, line starts lost):
 002-A-L1  ]herusale(m)?  [ends "herusale", final letter cut/absent]
 002-A-L2  ]aptiua fi   ["c" of captiua cut; "fi" with a mark above - possibly abbreviated "fi(lia)"? uncertain]
 002-A-L3  ]aañ. Po     [red "...a an̄." (an(tiphona)?) then black "Po"; the red letter before "an̄" is a cut "a" or other letter]
 002-A-L4  ]n ihe rusa  [i.e. "...n iherusa-"; read "in iherusa" with first letter cut]
 002-A-L5  ]nia. An̄    [red "An̄" (Ant(iphona)?), letters smudged]
 002-A-L6  ]laudē ei(us)?  [last word "ei" with superscript mark, perhaps "ei(us)"]
 002-A-L7  ] quia ecce
 002-A-L8  [red, illegible traces along bottom edge]
Right column (right edge cut):
 002-A-R1  Sur[      [Sur(ge)? only "Sur" visible]
 002-A-R2  mus[
 002-A-R3  dn̄s [     ["dn̄s" = d(omi)n(u)s]
 002-A-R4-5  large red initial, D or O (2 lines high), rest cut
 002-A-R6  nid[  or  niu[ ?
 002-A-R7  P[ with long stroke - "Pl"/"Pa"? uncertain
 002-A-R8  [traces]

FRAGMENT B, left part (image-002.jpg, viewed via crop-02.jpg, 2x enlargement)
Observation: larger, more cursive gothic hand (bookhand/bastarda-like), red rubric lines; the black text between the rubric lines is almost entirely abraded or washed out - only ghost strokes. A horizontal crease/fold crosses about mid-height. Left edge shows small red marks at line starts (paragraph marks / line-initial touches). Probably an ordinal/rubric-heavy text (rubrics seem to give liturgical directions) - tentative interpretation only.
 002-B-1 (red, top edge)  q(ui)?us? lc̄ q̄ta? sic[   [first word "q" + "us"-like, uncertain; "lc̄" = l(e)c(tio)?; third word "q" with superscript - q(ua)r(ta)? / q(uin)ta?; last "sic" or "lic" cut]
 002-B-2..5  black text, illegible (abraded); red dot/touch at left margin of lines ~2 and ~4
 002-B-6 (red)  ]an nesciuit? / ne sciuit?   [read "an nesciuit" - letters n-e-s-c-i-u-i-t uncertain, could be "nesciunt"]; another red letter at right edge cut
 002-B-7  black, illegible; a red "i" / stroke at left
 002-B-8 (red)  noct̄z? ꝛ officio[   ["no" + "tt"/"ct" + "z"-like abbreviation; then Tironian et (ꝛ) and "officio" cut at right]

FRAGMENT B, centre (image-003.jpg = upper-right quadrant of face 1; overlaps image-002 on the left part of fragment B; viewed via crop-03.jpg). The fragment is patched/backed with translucent strips (tape-like repairs) across its middle, which further obscure the black text. Lines continue those of image-002 (same physical lines; overlapping words noted, not double-counted).
 003-B-1 (red)  [overlap: ]lc̄ q̄ta sic] Ame?t? sing̃ animo(?)·    [after "sic": a word read "Ame-t"/"Amet"/"Arit" - uncertain, letters A-m/r-e/i-t; then "sing" with superscript stroke + horizontal stroke below g = sing(u)l(?)/sing(ulariter?) - abbreviation unresolved; then "Anim" + o/e/s-like letter + mark; perhaps "anime" or "animo"]
 003-B-2 (black) ]dem   [then very faint "  ...  " ; traces of 2 more words illegible]
 003-B-3 (black) ]mi c? / ]mi t   [short]
 003-B-4 (black) ]ui   [then later grey pencil "Frg" (modern, not part of the text)]; faint "en" / "cu" further right
 003-B-5 (black) illegible; modern grey pencil number "1834?" / "183 4n"? over the text (shelf/inventory mark; uncertain digits)
 003-B-6 (red)  [ne]sciuit? algorithmū·   [overlap with 002-B-6; second word read clearly as "algorithm" + final minims with macron: "algorith(m)ū"/"algorithmi"; final dot]
 003-B-7 (black) illegible, a "c"/"e" visible
 003-B-8 (red)  ꝛ officio· xii·? mensium·   [overlap "ꝛ officio" with 002-B-8; numeral read "xii" or "xu" with dots; then "mensium" (m-e-n-s-i-u-m, minims ambiguous) cut at bottom edge]

FRAGMENT B, right end (image-003.jpg, viewed via crop-04.jpg, 3x). Observation: at the right end of fragment B (past the large-script area) there is a block of much smaller, more cursive brown-ink script, ~16-18 short lines, with reddish touches/initial at its left edge (a red round initial, C/O-like, about a third of the way down). Its lines are much more closely spaced than the rubric/text lines of the main block, so it is either a second column in a smaller hand / commentary column, or a separate piece pasted on (the translucent repair strips run across both) - cannot tell from this image. Very faint; readings highly uncertain:
 003-Bright-1  ]xxx? ꝑ? e[      [numeral-like "xxx"?]
 003-Bright-2  ]na? dixit? [   [a "D"-like capital + "ixit"? uncertain]
 003-Bright-3  ]ab ? the(?)ge?  [illegible mostly]
 003-Bright-4  ]a fiendi? t ? x[
 003-Bright-5  in anno bis(sextili?)[   ["in anno" fairly likely; next word begins "bis"/"bif" - expansion only a guess, leave as "bis.."]
 003-Bright-6  fin? hora? s? m[
 003-Bright-7  ]na? ? ? ? [
 003-Bright-8  red initial C/O + ]? uua?[   [illegible]
 003-Bright-9..18  illegible traces; ~line 10 "q ...nite?" ; ~line 16 "? ? hora? ? ?" - not reliable.

FRAGMENT C, lower part (image-004.jpg = lower-left quadrant of face 1; viewed via crop-05.jpg, 2x, and crop-06.jpg, 5x on the red words). Image-002 shows the top of the strip (overlap).
Observation: long narrow curved strip, a vertical fold/crease runs along its length; sewing/nail holes near top and bottom. Text lines run ACROSS the strip (short line portions only), black ink almost entirely abraded.
 - Red gothic capital "D" (or "N"?) about 1/5 down this tile (image-004 approx y 260-330), one line high; no legible text beside it.
 - Black ink: only ghost strokes along the strip, illegible.
 - Red words, image-004 approx y 1000-1030: "ou? p(er)? ..e.." - two short red words, extremely faint and blurred at 5x; first word read "ou"/"cu"/"eii", second word begins with a long-descender letter (p/ꝑ/f) then 3-4 letters [illegible]. Unreliable.
 - Modern pencil inscription written along the strip's left edge (reading bottom-to-top): "Stams ? (A?) Frg 153 2n"? - letters "Stam..", then "Frg", then a number read "153" and "2n"/"2a"; a later shelf/inventory note, not text of the manuscript. Transcribed only as seen; digits uncertain.
 - Bottom tip: a black ink letter or two ("x"?), illegible.

image-005.jpg (lower-right quadrant of face 1): background only, no fragment, no text.

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE 2 (image-006.jpg, reduced overview): the same three fragments, apparently turned over (versos), laid out in the same arrangement.
  (A') small scrap, upper left: dense black textura with red; small format; one column of text visible with red marks; appears rotated (text may run vertically) - check on tile.
  (B') wide fragment, upper right: three large red initials/paragraph marks along the left side (at top, middle, lower), black text in a small gothic hand across, with a horizontal crease; a vertical fold line about 2/3 across.
  (C') curved strip: lines of small black text across the strip, red touches, modern pencil writing near lower part along the edge.
Tiles image-007..010 should be quadrants of this face.

FRAGMENT A' (image-007.jpg = upper-left quadrant of face 2; viewed via crop-07.jpg, 4x). Same textura and red as fragment A. Only one column portion visible (the scrap seems to show the part of the column under, at least, one edge cut both sides). Heavy show-through of the other side's script (large dark mirrored letters in the middle of the scrap, incl. a reversed tall form) - I have not counted those as text of this face.
 007-A'-1  ]ui,ues? ii[   [top line cut through, letters partly lost; reading weak]
 007-A'-2  ]ectaui(?)· + red C[   ["...ectau" + small superscript/mark, then a dot, then red round C/E capital cut at right]
 007-A'-3  (red) ]a·a? e? [  [red letters faint, illegible]
 007-A'-4  (red) ]Aeni? / Ant[  [red, faint; "A" + 3-4 letters]
 007-A'-5  Olite[    [initial O-like capital (or D) + "lite"; letter before it is lost to the left; red traces at left edge]
 007-A'-6  ]q(ui)s ad   [or "quia ad"/"qui ad"; the middle letter obscured by show-through]
 007-A'-7  ]humana? / ]hiumna?  [minims ambiguous; read "humana" tentatively]
 007-A'-8  ]aris u[  or ]arif in[   [bottom line, half cut]

FRAGMENT B', left part (image-007.jpg, viewed via crop-08.jpg, 2x).
Observation: a column of small, faded brown gothic text on the left (~14-16 lines visible, line starts cut at left edge), then to its right a vertical series of large red flourished initials (four visible: at top, two together near mid-height, and one/two at the bottom), each a round-bowled letter (E/C/G-like) with a long horizontal hairline flourish ending in serrations to the right, all linked by a vertical dashed red line. These look like the initials of a second column (or of entries) whose black text is faded to near-nothing. Horizontal crease just below mid-height.
Left column (very faint; readings low-confidence):
 007-B'-1  ]? ? ? [
 007-B'-2  ]o ?? ? ecce?   [last word "ecce"/"ccce" uncertain]
 007-B'-3  ]u?? ? la? de?   
 007-B'-4  brown-ink capital Q/O + "uantum"? / "atuitur"? [illegible beyond the capital; leave as "Q? ...ui.."]
 007-B'-5  ]fecta? ue?  / "pfecta" - p with stroke = p(er)fecta? uncertain
 007-B'-6..10  illegible traces (a "b"/"d" with long ascender in l.7; "u" in l.8)
 007-B'-11 ]ut? ? ? ... 
 007-B'-12 ]? ? ? [ ; lower lines illegible.
I could not get connected text from this face of B; contrast is too low at native resolution.

FRAGMENT B', centre/right (image-008.jpg = upper-right quadrant of face 2; overlaps image-007 at the red initials on the left; viewed directly and via crop-09.jpg, a 2x autocontrast crop - the contrast boost did not help much).
Observation: to the right of the red initials (their flourishes extend into this column), a column of black/brown gothic text, more cursive than fragment A, ~9 lines visible, mostly abraded; a vertical fold/repair strip at about 1/2 width and translucent tape repairs at right; horizontal crease at mid-height. A modern grey/blue pencil note "Frg / 153 1v"? in the lower left of this column (inventory mark, digits uncertain) - not text.
 008-B'-1  ]? lect? de c[ ... ]? ? ? n?[   [read "lect(?) de" after initial; the rest illegible]
 008-B'-2  ]? ? ina? ni(?)? [ ... ] ? ega? ? fu[  
 008-B'-3  ]? ? ? bra? [ ... ] ? e? ? ?anu[
 008-B'-4  ]? nue? ?gus? [
 008-B'-5  ]? ? uerē? / "ueru(m)"? [   [heavy letters, read u-e-r + 2 minims with mark]
 008-B'-6  illegible (just below crease)
 008-B'-7  ]? ? ? ?? ad liber[  [read "ad liber..." / "ad libe..." in right half]
 008-B'-8  ]? ? ? Vnq(ue)? / Vnde? me?[   [capital-like V/U + "nq" with mark]
 008-B'-9  ]? ? ? Atq(ue)? ce?[   ["Atq" + mark, fairly visible]
 008-B'-10 traces at bottom edge, red tinge (red text?) illegible.

FRAGMENT C' (image-009.jpg = lower-left quadrant of face 2; upper portion viewed via crop-10.jpg, 3x).
Observation: the strip carries short line-portions of a small brown gothic text running across the strip (~30+ lines down its length), a red initial (E/C-like, one-two lines high) near the top, a red small "P"/"b"-like letter lower down at the right of the text, and red-tinged letters near the bottom of the written area. A modern pencil note on a paper/parchment patch along the right edge, reading (bottom-to-top) "Stams, STA?, Frg. 153, 2v"? (digits/letters uncertain) - inventory mark, not text.
Upper portion (crop-10.jpg): line-ends only, 2-4 letters each, faded; I can see shapes like "ce", "ad", "tis", "ula", "tl?" but nothing I can read with confidence. Recorded as [illegible] after close inspection.
Lower written portion (image-009.jpg approx y 560-950; crop-11.jpg, 3x). Line fragments, 1-3 words wide, readings low-confidence:
 009-C'-a  ]i ?d?     
 009-C'-b  ]ca? s?
 009-C'-c  ]? ? ?gt? / ]ug?
 009-C'-d  ]? ? ? ru?d
 009-C'-e  red small letter "A"/"H" with red dot before it (paragraph sign / rubric letter)
 009-C'-f  ]a? b? ? a?
 009-C'-g  ]? ad ? ?
 009-C'-h  ]ras? Simg? / Bng?   [capital-like letter + "ng"? uncertain]
 009-C'-i  ]? ? m? ? 
 009-C'-j  ]e? ? ? uiro?
 009-C'-k  ]? ? r? ?
 009-C'-l  (red-tinged) ? ? ? ollo? / ollu?
No connected text could be secured from this strip.

image-010.jpg (lower-right quadrant of face 2): background only, no text.

SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- Three physically separate scraps per face, probably from at least two different manuscripts (A: small liturgical-looking textura with red rubrics "an̄"; B and C: larger gothic hands with red rubrics/flourished initials). Whether B and C belong together is not determinable from these images.
- Best-secured readings: fragment A lines "]herusale", "]aptiua fi", "an̄. Po", "]n ihe rusa", "An̄", "]laudē ei(us)?", "quia ecce", right col "Sur[", "mus", "dn̄s"; A' "Olite", "q(ui)s ad", "]humana?"; fragment B red rubrics "lc̄ q̄ta sic ... sing̃ animo(?)", "[ne]sciuit? algorithmū·", "ꝛ officio· xii·? mensium·"; B' "Atq(ue)", "ad liber[".
- Black text of B, B', C, C' is mostly abraded; translucent repair strips obscure parts of B/B'. No connected 10-line span could be read on any face; a raking-light or multispectral image of B and C would be needed.
- Modern pencil inventory notes ("Frg", "153", "Stams"?) are visible on B and C; transcribed as seen, not used for identification.
- Unread: B' right portion (illegible), C' upper half (illegible), B right-end small-script block beyond the first ~8 lines.
- Beyond the rules: I ran `ls` on the packet directory and `sips` for image dimensions, and used Python/PIL to make crops (crop-01.jpg to crop-11.jpg) in my scratch folder. Did not stop on the image limit.
